target.title: fix(brave): resolve env secret refs for search key
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Brave web search accepted configured API keys, but env-backed SecretRefs in `tools.web.search.apiKey` were not resolved through the shared web-search credential path before falling back to `BRAVE_API_KEY`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Brave provider should treat direct API keys, env SecretRefs, and provider fallback env vars consistently with the shared web-search credential contract. This change routes Brave credential resolution through the existing shared resolver instead of duplicating a literal-only read.

## User Impact

Users can configure Brave web search with an env SecretRef and have it used without live-key tests or custom provider-auth behavior. Existing `BRAVE_API_KEY` fallback behavior remains intact.

## Evidence

- Changed `extensions/brave/src/brave-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`.
- Added a regression in `extensions/brave/src/brave-web-search-provider.test.ts` proving a configured env SecretRef supplies the request auth header ahead of `BRAVE_API_KEY`.
- Live open-PR conflict scan found no exact overlap on these touched files.

## Proof

- Rebased cleanly onto `upstream/main` at `fbcb7812cb`.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/brave/src/brave-web-search-provider.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`
- Earlier touched-file checks: `pnpm format:check`, `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json ...`, and Claude autoreview clean after Codex autoreview was blocked by local OpenAI API 401.
